readme:
# JBang

Support for [JBang](https://www.jbang.dev) scripts: single-file Java programs that declare their own dependencies with `//DEPS` comments and run without a build file. The extension feeds those dependencies to the Java language server, so a script gets the same completion, hover and diagnostics as a Maven or Gradle project, and adds code lenses to run it.

This is the unmodified extension published on Open VSX, pinned to a specific version and verified to work in Diode. It depends on Language Support for Java by Red Hat, which is installed together with it.

## What works in Diode

Open a `.java` file with a `//DEPS` line: the extension synchronizes the script with the language server, and imports from the declared artifacts resolve. The `Synchronize JBang` and `Run JBang` code lenses appear above the script; `Run JBang` runs it in a terminal. Typing a `//DEPS` coordinate completes group and artifact ids from Maven Central.

## What does not

`Debug JBang` needs a Java debugger, and Diode has none. The run buttons the extension puts into the editor title bar are not shown — run from the code lens or the command palette instead. Pasting a Maven `<dependency>` block does not convert it into a `//DEPS` line, and `jbang-catalog.json` is not validated against its schema.

## Requirements

`jbang` on your PATH (or its location in the `jbang.home` setting), and a JDK for the language server — see Language Support for Java.
